title: Dependability Sprint Mosaic: SLO Onramp & Cross-Team Cadence Experiments
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, cross-functional experimental plan (the "Mosaic") to onboard 3 product areas onto a standard SLO cadence and observability surface. Goal is to validate a minimal, repeatable onramp that teams can use to define, measure, and iterate SLOs with platform guardrails — without heavy process overhead.

Background / motivation:
- We keep seeing long negotiation cycles and inconsistent signal definitions when services try to adopt SLOs.
- Heavy playbooks are hard to apply to small product teams; need a small-step experiment to build muscle memory.
- Platform can offer templates, dashboards, and a fast-feedback cadence that reduces friction and clarifies tradeoffs.

Scope (MVP):
- Run 6-week experiments with 3 participating feature teams (one infra-adjacent, two product features).
- Provide a single SLO template (availability + latency golden path) and a dashboard + alert wiring guide.
- Weekly 30-minute sync + fortnightly review with SRE/Platform to adjust thresholds and observability.

Key outcomes (hypotheses to test):
1) Teams can define an initial SLO and associated signal within 2 weeks using the template.
2) A weekly lightweight sync reduces time-to-remediation for incidents that affect the SLO by >25%.
3) Platform-provided dashboards + pre-baked queries lead to consistent incident postmortems and fewer ambiguous RCA threads.

Experiment timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): onboarding call, access checks, dashboard cloning, ticket templates created.
- Week 1–2 (onramp): teams draft SLOs, create metrics in dashboards, initial baseline analysis.
- Week 3–4 (observe & tune): run against live traffic, tune error budget burn rules, collect raw incident signals.
- Week 5 (simulate): inject low-impact spike tests / traffic skew and observe SLO behavior.
- Week 6 (retro + decision): determine whether to iterate, adopt, or revert.

Roles & responsibilities (minimal):
- Product team lead: owns SLO definition + acceptance criteria.
- Eng owner (feature): implements metrics and tags traffic.
- Platform eng (Aisha): provides dashboard templates, query snippets, runbook skeletons.
- SRE liaison (Marco): validates thresholds, advises on safe remediation playbooks.
- Customer Success (optional): review user-facing SLAs if product team wants to align.

Deliverables:
- SLO spec (one-pager) per team — title, owner, metric, SLO target, measurement window, how to measure.
- Dashboard + alert wiring PR in their repo.
- Runbook entry: triage steps and fallback model variant (if applicable).
- Post-experiment retro notes and decision (adopt/iterate/reject).

Lightweight SLO template (to be copied into team docs):
- Name: <service> - golden-path availability
- Metric: requests_with_success_status / total_golden_path_requests (labelled by route)
- Target: 99.5% over rolling 30d (example; teams choose after baseline)
- Error budget burn policy: alert at 50% burn in 7d and 90% burn in 24h
- Owner & escalation path: name + pager/team

Observability & dashboards:
- Minimal set: rolling-30d SLO percentage, burn rate (7d & 24h), raw request rate, tail-latency p95/p99 for golden path.
- Platform will provide Grafana clone + prebuilt queries and a dashboard cloning script.

Communications & cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync: status updates, blockers, one ask/one offer format.
- Fortnightly review: deeper analysis, threshold proposals.
- Slack channel: #dependability-mosaic (read-only bot for dashboard links + burn alerts).

Decision criteria (end of 6 weeks):
- Adopt: team keeps SLO, minimal changes and a plan for operational ownership.
- Iterate: SLO kept as experiment for another cycle after adjustments.
- Revert: remove SLO monitoring if signals are misleading and cost > benefit, with documented reasons.

Risk & mitigations:
- False positives / noisy signals: provide sampling guidance and label hygiene docs.
- Over-alerting: enforce a default alert cooldown and require a human review before paging for first 2 alerts.
- Platform bandwidth: limit experiment cohort to 3 teams and cap work to 2 full days of platform effort per week.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- How to map golden-path routes for serverless-backed features? (Elena to prototype an instrumentation approach)
- Minimal cost guardrail: what query frequency keeps dashboards accurate but cheap? (Priya to draft cost estimates)
- Policy for automatic rollback of alerts that generate >50% false positives in 14 days.

Sample tickets (templates to clone):
- PLAT-ONRAMP-001: Clone dashboard and wire metrics for <team>/<service>
- PLAT-ONRAMP-002: Draft SLO one-pager for <service>
- PLAT-ONRAMP-003: Configure burn-rate alerts + add to runbook

Next steps (this week):
- Aisha: spin up dashboard clones + share script (ETA 2026-01-14)
- Marco: schedule weekly sync cadence invite and prepare threshold guidance doc (ETA 2026-01-15)
- Teams: commit to a 2-week onramp slot and create initial SLO one-pager draft (ETA 2026-01-19)

Notes to self / conversational fragments:
- keep onboarding light: example-driven > theory-driven.
- prefer concrete signal names over abstract definitions.
- avoid baked-in strict SLAs in pilot; we want teams to find the right target.

Appendix: quick links & helpers
- dashboard-clone-script: github PR above (copy & run)
- SLO one-pager template: confluence:CONF-REL-ONRAMP-001
- Suggested reading: SRE book chapters on error budgets (link in Confluence)

If reviewers: please comment inline where you think thresholds are too conservative or where instrumentation will be the blocker.
